# Kayode Adeniyi

> Kayode Adeniyi is a PhD researcher at Imperial College London working on uncertainty quantification for AI and sensing systems: how far a measurement or a model's answer can be trusted, and what that trust is worth to a decision. His work spans flood mapping and forecasting in data-scarce regions, AI for Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo, reliable data for AI agents, and AI policy.

Kayode is a member of the Schmidt Sciences Virtual Institute for Earth's Water (VIEW) at Imperial College London, supervised by Professor Wouter Buytaert, with fieldwork in Ghana. He holds an MSc with Distinction from the London School of Economics (Chevening Scholar) and a BSc from the University of Ilorin, Nigeria. He has worked as an AI Research Engineer at the London School of Economics, an AI Policy Analyst at the United Nations Development Programme, Head of Research and Innovation at the Geohazards Risk Mapping Initiative, and a Software Engineer at Flutterwave.

Contact: k.adeniyi26@imperial.ac.uk

## Projects

- [ng-flood](https://github.com/Adeniyikayodee/ng-flood): Google flood forecasts checked for any location in Nigeria, grouped by postcode area
- [Community-sensed flood warning](https://github.com/Adeniyikayodee/Reliability-Caps): Flood warnings for dense settlements from foundation-model embeddings and residents' reports
- [WazoCore](https://github.com/Adeniyikayodee/WazoCore): Vocabulary expansion of N-ATLaS for faster Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo generation
- [gagelink](https://github.com/Adeniyikayodee/gagelink): MCP server giving AI agents river and flood data with units and datums attached
- [Katcha Ward flood study](https://www.preventionweb.net/publication/documents-and-publications/flood-tolerant-rice-seed-deployment-and-satellite-based): Satellite flood risk assessment for rice farmers, Niger State
